summary: Preserved the candidate's valid eager host serialization and corrected its CUDA-graph bypass by excluding custom all-reduce during active capture and rejecting direct capture-time launches. The exact candidate fails the graph contract regression and the correction passes. Native polling remains unbounded because this ROCm-only assignment cannot justify or validate a CUDA device deadline.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate lacks capture-time selection refusal and direct-launch rejection.
Both communicator implementations refuse selection during capture and the guard rejects direct capture-time launch.
Twelve eager serialization, host-thread locking, capture refusal, and adjacent capability tests passed.
On gfx950, two host threads and two GPU streams produced ordered numeric result 2, matching CPU reference 2.
A real HIP graph capture rejected the custom-AR guard call and left its stream/event state unchanged.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 executed the eager ordering and graph-capture guard probes; no custom all-reduce kernel or distributed workload was executed.
remaining_limitations: The assigned host has one AMD gfx950 GPU, not two NVIDIA A100 CUDA GPUs with NVLink and green contexts.
The original distributed CUDA deadlock and concurrent replay of two CUDA graphs were not executable.
The JIT one-shot push poll and legacy AOT barriers remain unbounded; no CUDA timeout was added without compiler, ISA, and runtime validation.
No model weights or full serving workload were used.
